title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative: In 2023, the Tourism Secretariat government of the state of Bahia has created a professional training program to promote the inclusive tourism sector. The program focus is on transgender individuals who are excluded from the labour market. The program aims to train more than 200 people in the capital by the end of 2023 and be expanded to other locations in 2024. The methodology is adapted to this audience in terms of time, strategy, and other important components for development, such as expression, art, and interpersonal relationships. The Brazilian Service to Support Micro and Small Companies (SEBRAE) trained groups of women from the Carnauba production chain received training in handicraft activities as an alternative source of income (March, 2023). These women belong to carnauba extractor families with low family income, highly vulnerable to inadequate working conditions. The entire mobilization of the beneficiary groups relied on the support and participation of the Rural Workers Union of the municipalities served. In total, 24 women from two municipalities in the state of Piauí received training on production management and sales. They have participated in fairs and events to promote the sale of their products, generating income for their families. The SENAI developed innovative skills programmes for entepreneurship with blended learning programmes for migrant women vulnerable to forced labour in the Mato Grosso state. During2023, the Pastoral Center for Migrants (CPM) successfully forged partnerships with local training institutions such as SENAI - National Service for Industrial Training, enabling the provision of five courses for 105 migrant women. These courses aimed to equip them with skills and empower them in their entrepreneurial pursuits. The courses offered were as follows: Technical Introduction for Manicure and Pedicure, Eyebrow Design and Egyptian Waxing, Eyelash Extensions, Housekeeping, and Handmade Cleaning Products. The public policy was developed with direct support and implementation by the ILO. The best practices used to design the policy were those developed by ILO in recent years. The ILO will enter a cooperation agreement with the tourism secretariat of the state of Bahia by the end of 2023 to formalize the partnership in the inclusion tourism policy. The entire strategy for identifying, mobilizing and raising awareness of the beneficiaries served was coordinated by the ILO from the beginning. The ILO's strategic vision on the gender issue was important to highlight the female potential in generating income for the family, since the carnauba production chain is mostly occupied by the male workers. The ILO also worked to facilitate a partnership with SEBRAE - Brazilian Service to Support Micro and Small Companies. The ILO played a pivotal role in facilitating the partnership between SENAI and CPM to provide entrepreneurship courses specifically designed for migrant women in Mato Grosso. This collaboration marked a significant milestone for the CPM, as it expanded its range of services to include entrepreneurship training, which had not been offered before. Furthermore, the gender approach introduced by the ILO was a novel concept for the CPM, highlighting the organization's commitment to addressing the unique challenges faced by migrant women. By incorporating a gender perspective into the courses, the CPM aimed to empower and support women in their entrepreneurial endeavors, promoting gender equality and women's economic empowerment. Furthermore, the enhancement of CPM's physical infrastructure (provided through the Implementation Agreement signed with the ILO), allowed for the majority of the training sessions to take place within the CPM premises. This arrangement proved beneficial for migrant women who were residing at the CPM, as it eliminated the concern of leaving their children unattended while attending the courses.

description.narrative: In July 2023, Brazil adopted a law (14.611, 2023) guaranteeing wage equality between men and women. Measures to promote wage and salary equality between man and women are also provided for in the new legislation. These measures include the promotion and implementation of diversity and inclusion programs in the workplace, which entails training for managers, leaders, and employees on the topic of gender equity in the labour market fostering for equal opportunities of women in entering, remaining, and advancing in the labour market alongside men. This law is an effort to bring national legislation in line with ILO Convention No. 100. The ILO conducted a series of technical meetings with the Ministry of Women and the Ministry of Labour (since February 2023) to support the discussion for alignment with ILO Convention No. 100. As part of the effort, Brazil has joined the Equal Pay International Coalition (EPIC) and has been receiving technical support from the ILO to enhance its laws and policies.

description.narrative:
The Child Labour Complaint System, inspired by the Ipê System on forced labour complaints, was adopted and launched by the Secretariat for Labour Inspection in May 2022. The system has allowed the enhancement of the process of receiving complaints and expediting their handling, enabling more efficient actions through improved management, planning, and investigation of the received information, generating significant improvements. The ILO provided technical support to develop the new complaint system for registering child labour complaints and it was launched during the V Global Conference on Child Labour (15-20 May 2022).
The ILO has actively engaged in a working group established by the Labour Inspection to collaboratively develop the CL Complaint System. Additionally, the ILO has provided support for the system's development. The Ministry of Labour recognizes the ILO's significant contribution to the system's creation and has featured the ILO logo on the system's main page.
